name: CA-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+9 partisan lean favors the Democratic nominee
Jacqui Irwin's large fundraising and cash advantage over Sam Gallucci
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot adds uncertainty
Prediction markets price the Democrat near 95%
model.rationale: The district's D+9 lean and a favorable national environment point to a Democratic hold, and Irwin has outraised Gallucci by more than two to one with a large cash-on-hand edge. The open-seat nature and absence of polling argue for trimming the expected margin somewhat below the fundamentals-based estimate.
model.watch: A late outside-spending surge for Gallucci or a strong top-of-ticket Republican environment in California could narrow the race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Julia Brownley (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Julia Brownley's retirement leaves this Ventura County-area seat open, but the district's D+9 partisan lean keeps it on Democratic turf. Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin enters as the Democratic nominee with a clear financial edge, having raised roughly $820,000 and holding about $295,000 on hand, while Republican Sam Gallucci has raised about $377,000 with only $34,000 in the bank. Outside spending has so far favored Irwin, with no reported opposition spending against her.

Prediction markets price the Democrat at roughly 95%, and no general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and money. The race is best characterized as Likely Democratic, with the open-seat dynamic the main source of uncertainty.
